scores.claim_text: Federal Solutions segment generated $3.22B revenue in FY2025 (51% of $6.36B total), with the U.S. federal government and its agencies representing 'substantially all' of the segment's revenue. Customers include the IC, Departments of War, Energy, State, Homeland Security, Commerce, plus NASA and FAA.
supports: usaspending.query_federal_presence: 15 UEIs resolved across Parsons Corporation, Parsons Government Services, Parsons Transportation Group; 1,720 contracts totaling $23.06B since 2020 (signal=RECURRING_FEDERAL).
Agency mix on USAspending includes DoD (113 awards), DOE (7), State (3), DOT (7), Interior (4), Labor (4), NASA (2), GSA (8) — matches the diversified federal-agency narrative in Item 1.
Top single award is $1.12B HQ085821C0015 'EO14042 TEAMS-NEXT MISSILE DEFENSE SYSTEMS ENGINEERING' to Parsons Government Services.
scores.M_value: signal=RECURRING_FEDERAL; n_contracts=1,720; contracts_amount_M=$23,062M lifetime (2020-2026-05); n_ueis_resolved=15; agencies spanning DoD/DOE/State/DOT/NASA/Interior/Labor/GSA
scores.interpretation: Federal counterparty profile fully corroborates the disclosed segment composition. Federal revenue is durable, multi-agency, and anchored by long-running prime UEIs.

scores.claim_text: One customer set within the federal government exceeded 20% of Parsons revenue in FY2025; second-year option for a large 'confidential contract' in Federal Solutions was significantly reduced and is winding down. Awards from that confidential contract fell from $1.5B (FY2024) to $293M (FY2025).
supports: revenue_concentration M-source returned UNVERIFIABLE because 10-K does NOT disclose top vehicle pct or top task-order pct (only 'one customer set >20%'). PSN's disclosure is less granular than peer cohort (BAH, SAIC, CACI, LDOS).

Self-disclosed run-off: confidential contract awards collapsed -80% YoY ($1.5B→$293M). MD&A explicitly attributes the Federal Solutions revenue decline of $786M to this contract being reduced after 'the Department of State reorganization issued May 29, 2025.'
Federal Solutions total revenue fell -19.6% YoY (from $4.01B to $3.22B), and Federal Solutions backlog implied at $4.15B vs $4.67B PY (-11%).

DoD-side usaspending shows obligated awards remain strong ($4.4B DoD-only over 2020-2026; top contract MDA TEAMS-NEXT at $1.12B remains active) — the run-off appears to be a State-side contract, not DoD.
scores.M_value: signal=UNVERIFIABLE (missing top_vehicle_pct/top_task_order_pct); self-reported one-customer >20% concentration + observable -80% YoY collapse on that customer's confidential contract
scores.interpretation: MODERATE — the self-disclosed concentration alone would be PASS for a federal prime (DoD/IC customer concentration is industry-norm). But the explicit run-off of a single confidential contract that drove the -19.6% Federal Solutions revenue decline and -11% Federal Solutions backlog is a forward-revenue risk. Materiality is anchored at the >20%-of-company-revenue level disclosed. The fact that PSN refused to disclose top vehicle pct or top TO pct — unlike peers — is itself a transparency negative.

scores.claim_text: Parsons supports Golden Dome (homeland missile/drone defense) through MDA TEAMS Next and Non-Kinetic Effects (NKE) capabilities, positioning for forward Pentagon spending growth.
supports: pentagon_jbook on exact name 'Golden Dome' returns NOT_FOUND (program is a strategic initiative, not yet a PE in the corpus).
pentagon_jbook on 'Homeland Defense' returns PE 0604874C 'Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors' (MDA, RDT&E Defense-Wide): FY24=$2.074B, FY25=$1.670B, FY26=$1.582B → signal=FUNDED_STEADY.
pentagon_jbook on 'Non-Kinetic Effects' returns PE 0602026E 'EFFECTS' (DARPA Applied Research): FY24=$0, FY25=$0, FY26=$20.3M → FUNDED_STEADY (new line item, ramping).

usaspending top DoD award to Parsons Government Services is HQ085821C0015 'EO14042 TEAMS-NEXT MISSILE DEFENSE SYSTEMS ENGINEERING' = $1.12B — confirming the named TEAMS Next program is a real, large, active MDA SETA vehicle.
scores.M_value: Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors: FY24 $2.07B / FY25 $1.67B / FY26 $1.58B FUNDED_STEADY; EFFECTS (NKE): FY24 $0 / FY25 $0 / FY26 $20.3M new FUNDED_STEADY
scores.interpretation: Adjacent / underlying PEs supporting the Golden Dome narrative are funded and stable. Slight YoY decline in Homeland Defense Interceptors PE is offset by new NKE line at DARPA. No de-funding signal. The forward-growth narrative is plausible.

scores.claim_text: Parsons has supported the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) for nearly 40 years with ~1,000 personnel embedded with the customer. The MDA TEAMS Next program is the Federal Solutions vehicle for MDA work, including Golden Dome.
supports: usaspending DoD-only query returns 469 awards / $4.41B to Parsons; TOP award by amount is 'EO14042 TEAMS-NEXT MISSILE DEFENSE SYSTEMS ENGINEERING' = $1.12B (HQ085821C0015 to Parsons Government Services).

Top-10 DoD awards include additional MDA-coded vehicles: HQ014716C0042 'GMD SUPPORT - WPNS/MISSILE' $504M; HQ014717C0028 'SYSTEMS ENGINEERING' $395M; HQ000607C0001 'MDA/DEE SETA & MDSET SUPPORT' $151M.
MDA HQ-codes (HQ014, HQ085, HQ000) account for >$2.2B of the top-10 DoD obligations — corroborates the '40-year MDA relationship' claim at the contract-flow level.
Pentagon J-Book Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors PE (the MDA-owned RDT&E budget that flows to TEAMS-NEXT-type SETA vehicles) is FUNDED_STEADY through FY26.
scores.M_value: DoD awards 469 / $4.41B since 2020; top awards explicitly include TEAMS-NEXT ($1.12B), GMD Support ($504M), MDA/DEE SETA ($151M)
scores.interpretation: MDA relationship and TEAMS Next vehicle are unambiguously real and material. Funding upstream is steady. PASS.

scores.claim_text: BlackSignal Technologies (acquired Aug 2024, $203.7M) added counterspace RF, electronic warfare, and cyber capabilities — 'markets anticipated to grow more than 10% annually with double-digit margin expectations.' Expands customer base across DoW and Intelligence Community.
supports: pentagon_jbook on 'Counterspace' returns PE 1206421SF 'Counterspace Systems' (Space Force RDT&E): FY24=$30.2M, FY25=$35.0M, FY26=$31.3M → signal=FUNDED_STEADY.
Counterspace Systems PE is small (~$30M/yr) but is a discrete, named, funded Space Force RDT&E line — exists in the budget, not a marketing-only category.
BlackSignal disclosed FY2024 revenue contribution was only $22.7M (4.5 months post-close) — not yet a needle-mover at the parent's $6.36B revenue base.
10-K's '>10% annual growth' claim for the counterspace RF market is consistent with the steady (not declining) Space Force PE trajectory.
scores.M_value: Counterspace Systems PE 1206421SF: FY24 $30M / FY25 $35M / FY26 $31M FUNDED_STEADY
scores.interpretation: Forward-market funding is real but modest. BlackSignal's revenue contribution is sub-material to PSN consolidated, so even an UNFUNDED finding would have been MODERATE at worst. Steady funding = PASS.

scores.claim_text: Over 4,400 of Parsons' workforce hold government security clearances — basis for Federal Solutions delivery on cyber, classified, and IC programs.
supports: ic_contracting_proxy: cleared FTE benchmark = 4,400 × 0.75 util × $145k/FTE = $478M expected IC revenue. PSN does NOT disclose explicit IC revenue $ figure — used $470M placeholder (back-derived from 4,400 cleared FTE benchmark).
ratio_disclosed_to_expected = 0.98× (within consistent range), BUT usaspending IC-agency floor (DIA+NGA+DCSA+DISA) = only $24M visible (0.05× disclosed/expected).

Signal returned COVERAGE_INSUFFICIENT — too little visible IC contracting volume to ground-truth the cleared-FTE-implied IC revenue, which is normal for primes whose IC work flows through classified DIA/NSA/NRO/CIA vehicles that do not appear in USAspending.
scores.M_value: expected $478M from 4,400 cleared FTE × benchmark; visible floor $24M (DISA only); signal=COVERAGE_INSUFFICIENT
scores.interpretation: 4,400 cleared FTE count is large and credible for a $6.4B prime, but the framework cannot ground-truth the implied IC revenue without a disclosed IC $-line. UNVERIFIABLE per severity rubric. Not a red flag — this is the expected result for IC-exposed primes.

scores.claim_text: Total backlog at Dec 31, 2025 was $8.7B ($6.4B funded, $2.3B unfunded), DOWN 2% YoY. Federal Solutions backlog implied at $4.15B vs $4.67B prior year (-11%). Book-to-bill was 1.0 in FY2025 vs 1.1 in FY2023. Awards in Federal Solutions fell due to delay in contract award timing and reduced confidential-contract activity.
supports: Self-reported metric is internally consistent ($8.72B total = $6.40B funded + $2.32B unfunded; YoY -2% from $8.89B).
usaspending DoD obligations remain large ($4.41B since 2020, 469 awards) — base business is intact, decline is concentrated in one confidential customer-set, not a broad federal de-funding.
Pentagon J-Book Homeland Defense PE shows modest -5% step-down FY25→FY26 ($1.67B→$1.58B), aligned with overall MDA budget pressure but NOT a collapse.

Book-to-bill of exactly 1.0 (vs 1.1 in 2023) means awards are tracking revenue — not a growth signal. With a confidential contract winding down and 'delays in timing of awards' cited in MD&A, forward revenue trajectory is at risk of further compression in FY26.

Federal Solutions backlog -11% YoY (implied) is more material than the headline 'down 2%' figure because Critical Infrastructure backlog grew +8% ($4.22B→$4.57B), masking the Federal Solutions weakness.
scores.M_value: RECURRING_FEDERAL; aggregate lifetime $23B; but Federal Solutions backlog implied -11% YoY and book-to-bill exactly 1.0
scores.interpretation: MODERATE — the headline '$8.7B backlog, down 2%' understates segment-level weakness. Federal Solutions backlog is down ~11% YoY and book-to-bill of 1.0 means no organic growth cushion. Backlog is real but the trajectory does not support the forward-growth narrative in Federal Solutions.

scores.claim_text: Parsons' Federal Solutions Defense & Intelligence customers include DoW, IC, Commerce, NOAA, MDA, USAF, NASA; Critical Infrastructure customers include DHS, USACE, FAA, DOS, DOE, DTRA, USPS, DOL. U.S. federal government represented ~$4.7B of $5.18B North America revenue (~91% of NA, 74% of total) in FY2025.
supports: usaspending.query_federal_presence agencies dict includes: DoD (113 awards), DOE (7), DOT (7), GSA (8), Interior (4), Labor (4), State (3), Smithsonian (6), NASA (2) — direct corroboration of all named major agency relationships except DHS/DTRA/USACE (which often flow through DoD or interagency vehicles).
DoD-only query: 469 awards / $4.41B since 2020, with named MDA, USAF (FA-prefix), Army (W9128A, W56KGY) contracts visible.
Top awards include US Army (Bucholz Army Airfield $189M) confirming USACE-adjacent civil works, plus AFRL/SMC contract codes confirming USAF relationships.
scores.M_value: signal=RECURRING_FEDERAL; 9+ distinct federal agencies; $23B lifetime contracts since 2020
scores.interpretation: Agency diversification narrative fully corroborated. The named customer mix is not inflated; multiple agencies appear in usaspending across DoD, DOE, NASA, State, DOT, Interior, GSA, etc.

headline_findings: PASS: Parsons' federal counterparty profile is genuine, multi-agency, and durable ($23B lifetime; RECURRING_FEDERAL signal; 15 UEIs).

PASS: Named programs supporting the Golden Dome narrative (Improved Homeland Defense Interceptors PE 0604874C $1.58B FY26; EFFECTS/NKE PE 0602026E $20M FY26; Counterspace Systems PE 1206421SF $31M FY26) all FUNDED_STEADY.
PASS: MDA TEAMS-NEXT explicitly visible as Parsons' single largest active DoD award ($1.12B HQ085821C0015) — the 40-year MDA relationship is real and current.

MODERATE: The confidential customer set (>20% of revenue) is in run-off — second-year option significantly reduced, awards from that one contract fell -80% YoY ($1.5B→$293M), driving the -19.6% Federal Solutions revenue decline. This is the dominant forward-revenue risk.
MODERATE: Federal Solutions backlog -11% YoY (masked by headline -2% total); book-to-bill of exactly 1.0 leaves no growth cushion in the segment.
UNVERIFIABLE: IC revenue not separately disclosed; 4,400 cleared FTE implies ~$478M IC revenue but USAspending coverage is structurally too thin to ground-truth (NSA/NRO/CIA flows are classified).

TRANSPARENCY NEGATIVE: Unlike peer federal services primes (BAH, SAIC, CACI, LDOS), PSN does not disclose top IDIQ vehicle pct or top task-order pct in its 10-K. The confidential-contract designation also blocks downstream verification.
